title: Topological effects in the polarization of the Fulling-Rindler vacuum
authors: A. A. Saharian, G. V. Mirzoyan, V. S. Torosyan
abstract: We investigate how the compactification of some spatial dimensions in Rindler spacetime affects the vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of the field squared and the energy-momentum tensor for a charged scalar field prepared in the Fulling-Rindler vacuum state. A toral compactification is considered with quasi-periodicity conditions on the field operator along the compact dimensions. The phases of these conditions are interpreted in terms of the magnetic flux enclosed by the compact dimensions. For a general number of spatial dimensions, the components of the VEVs are explicitly separated, corresponding to the expectation values in the Minkowski vacuum. As a limiting case, the VEVs are retrieved in Rindler spacetime with trivial topology. We demonstrate that, for non-zero phases in the periodicity conditions, the vacuum energy-momentum tensor exhibits off-diagonal components with indices in the compact subspace. Near the Rindler horizon, the leading terms in the asymptotic expansions of the field squared and the diagonal components of the energy-momentum tensor coincide with the corresponding VEVs in Rindler spacetime with trivial topology. The off-diagonal components of the energy-momentum tensor vanish on the Rindler horizon. For small accelerations, the difference between the VEVs in the Fulling-Rindler and Minkowski vacua is exponentially small. The exception to this is a massless field with zero phases in the periodicity conditions. In this special case, the difference decays according to a power law as a function of acceleration. As an application, we consider the VEVs near the horizon of cylindrical black holes and topological black holes with toroidal horizons.
summary:
This paper analyzes the vacuum structure of a charged scalar field confined to Rindler spacetime with compactified dimensions. It calculates how topological effects, quantified by enclosed magnetic fluxes, modify the vacuum expectation values of observables like $\langle T_{\mu
u} angle$. The results highlight distinct decay behaviors—exponential versus power-law—depending on whether the field is massless and if the flux conditions are trivial.
main_problem: The study investigates how compactifying spatial dimensions within Rindler spacetime affects the vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of field observables for a charged scalar field.
main_result: The VEVs exhibit topological contributions dependent on enclosed magnetic fluxes, and the difference between Fulling-Rindler and Minkowski vacua is generally exponentially small unless the field is massless with zero phases, leading to power-law decay.
method: Calculations rely on evaluating vacuum expectation values using Hadamard functions and mode summation techniques, comparing results across different topological limits (Minkowski vs. Rindler).
model_or_system: The system models a charged scalar field in a $(D+1)$-dimensional spacetime that is locally Rindler, incorporating compact dimensions with quasi-periodicity conditions related to magnetic fluxes.
key_observables:
Vacuum expectation values of the field squared ($\langle \phi^2 angle$) and components of the energy-momentum tensor ($\langle T_{\mu
u} angle$).
important_parameters: Proper acceleration, compactification lengths ($L_l$), field mass ($m$), and enclosed magnetic fluxes ($\Phi_l$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a locally Rindler geometry and utilizes approximations in various asymptotic limits (e.g., near the horizon or for small accelerations).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the VEV of the field squared for massless fields showing dependence on acceleration/compactification parameters, comparing results to trivial topology cases.
paper_structure:
The paper analyzes the problem by first setting up the field equation and periodicity conditions; it then calculates $\langle \phi^2 angle$ and $\langle T_{\mu
u} angle$, deriving explicit forms for the topological contributions in different limits, and finally applying these results to physical scenarios like black hole horizons.
why_interesting: The study connects concepts from quantum field theory in curved spacetime (Rindler/Fulling-Rindler) with topology via magnetic fluxes, yielding non-trivial vacuum energy corrections that decay differently based on mass and flux conditions.
